# Goal

Test whether symbiont composition changed across sampling eras while accounting
for uneven sampling depth among eras.

This cleaned analysis uses post-MED ITS2 sequence variants only. Type profiles,
exploratory maps, old commented code, and temporary one-off exports were removed.
The working composition scale is symbiont clade/genus: `A`, `B`, `C`, `D`, and
`G`.

# Required input files

Copy these files from the previous project into the paths below.

```{r required-files}
required_files
```

```{r check-input-files}
missing_files <- required_files |>
  filter(!file.exists(path))

if (nrow(missing_files) > 0) {
  knitr::kable(missing_files, caption = "Files still needed before the analysis can run.")
  knitr::knit_exit()
}
```

# Load and clean data

```{r load-data}
metadata <- load_sample_metadata("metadata/decadalshifts_SST.xls")

variant_runs <- load_variant_runs(c(
  pawar = required_files$path[required_files$key == "pawar_variants"],
  conn = required_files$path[required_files$key == "conn_variants"]
))

sample_clades <- prepare_sample_clade_composition(
  metadata = metadata,
  variants = variant_runs,
  min_reads = 100
)

sample_retention <- audit_sample_retention(
  metadata = metadata,
  variants = variant_runs,
  min_reads = 100
)

readr::write_csv(sample_clades, "data/processed/sample_clade_composition.csv")
readr::write_csv(sample_retention$stage_counts, "outputs/tables/sample_retention_audit.csv")
readr::write_csv(sample_retention$dropped_samples, "outputs/tables/dropped_samples.csv")
```

```{r sample-summary}
sample_retention$stage_counts |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Sample retention audit")

if (nrow(sample_retention$duplicate_sample_names) > 0) {
  sample_retention$duplicate_sample_names |>
    knitr::kable(caption = "Sample names present in more than one imported run")
}

sample_summary <- sample_clades |>
  count(collection_subregion, host_species_code, era, name = "n") |>
  arrange(collection_subregion, host_species_code, era)

readr::write_csv(sample_summary, "outputs/tables/sample_counts_by_era.csv")

knitr::kable(sample_summary)
```

```{r drto-site-species-sample-summary}
drto_site_species_summary <- sample_clades |>
  filter(collection_subregion == "Dry Tortugas") |>
  count(
    collection_subregion, collection_site, host_species_code,
    host_genus, host_species,
    name = "n_samples"
  ) |>
  arrange(collection_site, host_species_code)

readr::write_csv(
  drto_site_species_summary,
  "outputs/tables/drto_its2_sample_counts_by_site_species.csv"
)

knitr::kable(
  drto_site_species_summary,
  caption = "Dry Tortugas ITS2 samples retained for the main analysis by site and species"
)
```

# Sampling depth diagnostics

```{r depth-diagnostics}
depth_summary <- sample_clades |>
  group_by(collection_subregion, host_species_code, era) |>
  summarize(
    n = n(),
    median_depth_ft = median(depth_ft, na.rm = TRUE),
    q25_depth_ft = quantile(depth_ft, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q75_depth_ft = quantile(depth_ft, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

readr::write_csv(depth_summary, "outputs/tables/depth_summary_by_era.csv")

ggplot(sample_clades, aes(x = era, y = depth_ft)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.35, size = 1) +
  facet_grid(collection_subregion ~ host_species_code, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Collection depth (ft)") +
  theme_classic()

ggsave("outputs/figures/depth_by_era.png", width = 11, height = 7, dpi = 300)
```

# Symbiont composition

For each subregion-by-species group, samples are binned by pooled depth. Within
each era, samples are weighted so the era depth-bin distribution matches the
pooled depth distribution for that subregion-by-species group. This preserves
the observed samples while reducing bias from eras being sampled at different
depths.

Dry Tortugas samples are not depth-standardized because one era lacks depth
information; for cross-era Dry Tortugas comparisons, all eras are therefore
kept on the same non-depth-standardized scale. Other subregion-by-species groups
without usable depth information are also kept and reported as
non-depth-standardized mean composition.

Groups with fewer than `min_n` samples in an era are retained with `NA`
composition for that era rather than silently dropped.

```{r standardized-composition}
min_n <- 4

composition_std <- standardized_era_composition(
  sample_clades,
  min_n = min_n,
  n_bins = 6,
  no_depth_standardization_subregions = "Dry Tortugas"
)

era_distances <- compare_eras(composition_std)

readr::write_csv(composition_std, "data/processed/depth_standardized_composition.csv")
readr::write_csv(era_distances, "outputs/tables/era_composition_distances.csv")

composition_std |>
  arrange(collection_subregion, host_species_code, era) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r composition-plot}
composition_long <- composition_std |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(clades), names_to = "clade", values_to = "proportion") |>
  filter(!is.na(proportion))

ggplot(composition_long, aes(x = era, y = proportion, fill = clade)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8, color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  facet_grid(collection_subregion + standardization_method ~ host_species_code) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Symbiont composition", fill = "Clade") +
  theme_classic()

ggsave("outputs/figures/depth_standardized_composition.png", width = 11, height = 7, dpi = 300)
```

```{r distance-plot}
era_distances_plot <- era_distances |>
  mutate(
    contrast = factor(
      paste(era1, "to", era2),
      levels = c("2001-03 to 2019-21", "2019-21 to 2024", "2001-03 to 2024")
    )
  )

ggplot(era_distances_plot, aes(x = contrast, y = Hellinger)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75) +
  facet_grid(collection_subregion ~ host_species_code) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Hellinger distance") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

ggsave("outputs/figures/era_hellinger_distances.png", width = 11, height = 7, dpi = 300)
```

# Statistical test

The primary test is a PERMANOVA on clade composition within each
subregion-by-species group. Groups with usable depth data are tested as:

`composition ~ era + depth_bin`

Groups without usable depth data are kept and tested as:

`composition ~ era`

These tests are paired with the composition summaries above so the biological
effect sizes are interpretable.

```{r permanova}
permanova_results <- permanova_by_group(
  sample_clades,
  min_n = min_n,
  permutations = 999,
  no_depth_adjustment_subregions = "Dry Tortugas"
)

readr::write_csv(permanova_results, "outputs/tables/permanova_by_subregion_species.csv")

permanova_results |>
  arrange(p_era) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

# ITS2 shifts versus experimental shuffling

The experimental shuffling coefficient table is joined by four-letter species
code. Two comparisons are produced:

1. era-to-era ITS2 composition distance versus experimental shuffling
   coefficient;
2. depth-standardized 2024 ITS2 clade-D proportion versus experimental clade-D
   proportion.

```{r experimental-comparison}
experimental_shuffling <- load_experimental_shuffling(
  required_files$path[required_files$key == "experimental_shuffling"]
)

experimental_comparison <- compare_its2_to_experimental(
  composition = composition_std,
  distances = era_distances,
  experimental = experimental_shuffling
)

readr::write_csv(
  experimental_comparison$distance,
  "outputs/tables/its2_distances_vs_experimental_shuffling.csv"
)
readr::write_csv(
  experimental_comparison$composition,
  "outputs/tables/its2_2024_clade_d_vs_experimental_prop_d.csv"
)
readr::write_csv(
  experimental_comparison$distance_correlations,
  "outputs/tables/correlations_its2_distances_vs_experimental_shuffling.csv"
)
readr::write_csv(
  experimental_comparison$composition_correlations,
  "outputs/tables/correlations_its2_2024_clade_d_vs_experimental_prop_d.csv"
)

experimental_comparison$distance_correlations |>
  arrange(collection_subregion, contrast) |>
  knitr::kable()

experimental_comparison$composition_correlations |>
  arrange(collection_subregion) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r experimental-distance-plot}
experimental_distance_plot <- experimental_comparison$distance |>
  filter(
    contrast == "2019-21 to 2024",
    !is.na(mean_shuff_coef),
    !is.na(Hellinger)
  )

ggplot(experimental_distance_plot, aes(x = mean_shuff_coef, y = Hellinger)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = experimental_n), alpha = 0.75) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = species_code),
    nudge_y = 0.02,
    check_overlap = TRUE,
    size = 3
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ collection_subregion) +
  labs(
    x = "Experimental shuffling coefficient",
    y = "ITS2 Hellinger distance (2019-21 to 2024)",
    size = "Experimental n"
  ) +
  theme_classic()

ggsave("outputs/figures/its2_distance_vs_experimental_shuffling.png", width = 9, height = 5, dpi = 300)
```

```{r experimental-clade-d-plot}
experimental_clade_d_plot <- experimental_comparison$composition |>
  filter(!is.na(mean_prop_d), !is.na(its2_prop_d_2024))

ggplot(experimental_clade_d_plot, aes(x = mean_prop_d, y = its2_prop_d_2024)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2, color = "grey55") +
  geom_point(aes(size = experimental_n), alpha = 0.75) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = species_code),
    nudge_y = 0.02,
    check_overlap = TRUE,
    size = 3
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ collection_subregion) +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  labs(
    x = "Experimental clade-D proportion",
    y = "Depth-standardized 2024 ITS2 clade-D proportion",
    size = "Experimental n"
  ) +
  theme_classic()

ggsave("outputs/figures/its2_2024_clade_d_vs_experimental_prop_d.png", width = 9, height = 5, dpi = 300)
```

# Across-region synthesis

This section combines Upper Keys and Dry Tortugas into one species-level view.
The inputs are the region-level compositions above: Upper Keys is
depth-standardized where possible, and Dry Tortugas is treated as
design-standardized by repeated site sampling and therefore not
depth-standardized.

Regions are weighted equally when both regions are available for a species and
era. This is intended as an across-region biological synthesis rather than a
sample-size-weighted summary dominated by the region with more samples.

```{r across-region-composition}
across_region_composition <- combine_regions_by_species(
  composition_std,
  regions = c("Upper Keys", "Dry Tortugas"),
  region_weighting = "equal"
)

across_region_distances <- compare_eras_by_species(across_region_composition)

readr::write_csv(
  across_region_composition,
  "data/processed/across_region_species_composition.csv"
)
readr::write_csv(
  across_region_distances,
  "outputs/tables/across_region_species_era_distances.csv"
)

across_region_composition |>
  arrange(host_species_code, era) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r across-region-composition-plot}
across_region_composition_long <- across_region_composition |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(clades), names_to = "clade", values_to = "proportion") |>
  filter(!is.na(proportion))

across_region_composition_plot <- ggplot(
  across_region_composition_long,
  aes(x = era, y = proportion, fill = clade)
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8, color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ host_species_code) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Across-region symbiont composition",
    fill = "Clade"
  ) +
  theme_classic()

across_region_composition_plot

ggsave(
  "outputs/figures/across_region_species_composition.png",
  across_region_composition_plot,
  width = 11,
  height = 7,
  dpi = 300
)
```

```{r across-region-experimental-comparison}
across_region_experimental <- compare_across_region_to_experimental(

)
readr::write_csv(

across_region_experimental$composition_correlations |>
```

```{r across-region-distance-experimental-plot}
across_region_distance_plot <- across_region_experimental$distance |>

ggplot(across_region_distance_plot, aes(x = mean_shuff_coef, y = Hellinger)) +
```
